subject: discussion on grouping with F2 data

messages.author: 756a884bb45d1384
messages.subject: discussion on grouping with F2 data
parts:
Hello Prof Dr. Broman,

I want to construct a genetic map using F2 data. I performed the analysis using following steps:

chr2 <- read.cross ("csv",dir = "","F2_data_map_contruction_ABH.csv", na.strings = c("-", "NA"), genotypes = c("A", "H", "B"), alleles = c("A", "B"), estimate.map =      FALSE )
gt1 <- geno.table(chr2)
todrop1 <- rownames(gt1[gt1$P.value < 0.0001,])
chr2 <- drop.markers(chr2, todrop1)
chr2 <- est.rf(chr2)
checkAlleles(chr2, threshold=5)
chr2 <- formLinkageGroups(chr2, max.rf=0.4, min.lod=30, reorgMarkers=TRUE)
png(filename="F2_map_RF.png", units="in", width=10, height=6.75, res=100)
plotRF(chr2)
dev.off()

As expected, I identified 11 linkage groups. But when I mapped those markers on the reference genome, I couldn't get any correlation between genetic and physical map. 


new_chr1234567891011
ChrA_v2.080921248688485749515146
ChrB_v2.09087897451575661434175
ChrC_v2.06356514644314376363132
ChrD_v2.05552363931393530356921
ChrE_v2.09478524642925141434726
ChrF_v2.0118907311968574857464837
ChrG_v2.07880466044434341853722
ChrH_v2.01861051069779948157825061
ChrI_v2.08667634739539939322929
ChrJ_v2.08874655699524143373731
ChrK_v2.01271568510880626763543948


Can you please explain what could be the issue?


Thanks and regards

Sandip

It beats me. I guess I'd look to see whether the marker names got misaligned.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: discussion on grouping with F2 data
parts:
I would look at the counts on the chromosomes and the order of markers’ chromosome assignments.
Also, compare the genotypes at a few markers to what’s in the originsl file. 
All presuming the marker names got misaligned at somepoint.

karl
